chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about one who confesses to the heirs for a debt upon himself while he is ill. He said: It is permissible upon him what he confesses to, if it is small.

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Confession or acknowledgment of a debt or right
key_terms.مَرِيضٌ: Sick or ill, specifically in the context of deathbed illness

ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a dying person's confession of debt to their heirs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a dying person's admission of debt to specific heirs is legally valid provided the amount is modest, reflecting the juristic principle that minor debts are less prone to the suspicion of favoritism or manipulation during the final illness (*marad al-mawt*). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing the rights of creditors with the equitable distribution of the estate, ensuring that small obligations do not disrupt the inheritance process. The distinction of 'smallness' (*qalilan*) serves as a safeguard against the common practice of debtors favoring certain heirs by attributing large debts to them before death.
